properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 4 at 7:49PM EDT until September 4 at 10:45PM EDT by NWS Raleigh NC
properties.description:
FFWRAH

The National Weather Service in Raleigh has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern Edgecombe County in central North Carolina...
Halifax County in central North Carolina...

* Until 1045 PM EDT.

* At 749 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 2 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Halifax, Scotland Neck, Enfield, Weldon, Hobgood, Tillery, South
Weldon and Medoc Mountain State Park.

This includes the following frequently flooded locations...
US Hwy 301 near Burnt Coat Swamp and Beech Swamp, Thirteen Bridges Rd
near Beech Swamp, NC Hwy 125 near Conoconnara Swamp and Hwy 258
between E 16th St and Lees Meadow Rd.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 4 at 7:54PM EDT until September 4 at 8:45PM EDT by NWS Wakefield VA
properties.description:
SVRAKQ

The National Weather Service in Wakefield has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Gates County in northeastern North Carolina...
The western City of Chesapeake in southeastern Virginia...
Central Isle of Wight County in southeastern Virginia...
The City of Suffolk in southeastern Virginia...

* Until 845 PM EDT.

* At 753 PM EDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from near Ivor to Windsor to 6 miles northwest of Gates,
moving east southeast at 25 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to trees and powerlines.

* Severe thunderstorms will be near...
Windsor, Holland, Suffolk, Gates, and Roduco around 800 PM EDT.
Isle Of Wight, Kings Fork, and Whaleyville around 805 PM EDT.
Downtown Suffolk around 810 PM EDT.
Sunbury and Corapeake around 820 PM EDT.
Chesapeake around 825 PM EDT.
Driver around 830 PM EDT.

Other locations impacted by these severe thunderstorms include
Carrollton, Longview, Benns Church, Savage, Topsy, Suffolk Airport,
Huntersville, Buckland, Dort, and Chuckatuck.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

Please report severe weather by calling 757-899-2415, posting to the
NWS Wakefield Facebook page, or using X @NWSWAKEFIELDVA.

drainage and low-lying areas.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 4 at 10:45AM CDT until September 5 at 12:44PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Menard Creek near Rye affecting Polk, Hardin and Liberty Counties.

For the Menard Creek...including Rye...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Menard Creek near Rye.

* WHEN...Until Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 23.0 feet, moderate lowland flooding begins as
low-lying areas along the creek are inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:15 AM CDT Friday the stage was 24.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 17.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:15 AM CDT Friday was 28.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage just
after midnight tonight and continue falling to 11.1 feet
Wednesday morning.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 24.6
feet on 03/12/2016.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/hgx.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1045 PM CDT.
